1.	Freshness & Variety

2.	Value for money / Wholesale rates

•	Ability to bargain.  ￼
3.	Additional services
•	Fish cleaning / cutting service available. Some vendors provide cleaning without extra cost or for a small charge.  ￼

4.	Location & accessibility

5.	Atmosphere
•	“Vibe” of a genuine fish market: lively, bustling; people like the authenticity.

featured_reviews.name: Sushil Malik
featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
Marve Beach is a treat for nature lovers! Me and my family loved visiting this spot for the stunning natural views and breathtaking sunsets 🌅. The road conditions leading to the beach are great, making it a smooth drive.

As we arrived in the first half, we stumbled upon a bustling fish market, and it was a real treat! The variety and freshness of the catch were impressive 🐟. We even picked up some fresh seafood to take home.

The beach itself is peaceful, with a lovely ambiance that's perfect for a family outing. The sunsets here are simply gorgeous, and we ended up spending hours soaking in the views.

While the beach is a bit rocky, it's not a major issue, and the natural beauty more than makes up for it. There are plenty of local eateries nearby serving delicious seafood and snacks 🍽️.

If you're looking for a relaxing day out with family, Marve Beach is a great choice! 😊 The atmosphere is chill, and the natural beauty is simply stunning.

Would definitely recommend Marve Beach to anyone looking for a lovely beach experience with great views and good vibes!"

featured_reviews.name: Noel Nadar
featured_reviews.review_text: Marve beach is located in Malad West. Last stop of 272 bus from Malad railway station to Marve beach. It's a good place to relax for sometime, there are eateries available at the beach. Ferry is available from Marve Beach to go to Manori. It's a less than 5 minutes ferry from Marve to Manori. Good place.

featured_reviews.name: stephen valdeiro
featured_reviews.review_text: Good service at 15 minutes interval available till midnight. It takes around 10/15  minutes for one way trip, depending on tides. A singer serenades during short trip.. Enjoyable

featured_reviews.name: Nahushraj Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Marve Jetty serves as one of the gateway connecting the mainland to Gorai Island through a quick ferry ride. The drive to the jetty from the surrounding suburbs is good but you might face traffic on weekends and on busy evenings.

Once you arrive, the beach area welcomes you with a vibrant stretch of food stalls offering everything from classic chaat to flavourful seafood preparations (must try fried fish). And if you’re someone who appreciates a truly fresh catch, consider buying fish from the local Koli community. Their produce is fresh, reasonably priced, and supports the traditional fishing families who have lived by these shores for generations.

Parking facilities have also improved greatly in recent times. Visitors will find ample and convenient parking space for both two-wheelers and four-wheelers, making the overall experience smooth and stress-free.

featured_reviews.name: pratyusha mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text: This jetty offers communication to Manor. The launch service is quite frequent in morning at interval of 5-10 mins and it costs around 15 rupees per head for the crossover. Charges are separate for vehicle like bike etc. The sea is a site to behold when visited in early mornings with gulls flying over the clean sea water reflecting early morning sun rays. There is toilet facility available in the jetty and many eateries too.

featured_reviews.name: Ragini Dev
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a woman living in the hustle of Mumbai, finding a pocket of peace is a luxury, and that's exactly what Marve Beach offers. It’s not about the thrill of water sports; it’s about the sheer calmness and clarity I find here.
I often visit in the late afternoon, and the primary appeal is the relative serenity. Unlike the constant commotion of Juhu or Chowpatty, Marve feels almost residential—a true suburban retreat. I appreciate that I can take a long, leisurely stroll barefoot without constantly bumping into crowds. It feels much safer and more comfortable to simply walk, reflect, and enjoy my own company here.
The highlight, without a doubt, is the sunset. Marve offers an absolutely unspoiled view of the sun sinking into the Arabian Sea. Watching the sky explode in shades of burnt orange and soft lavender while the tide gently laps the shore is truly a grounding experience. It’s a photographer’s dream and a perfect moment for a bit of personal meditation.
Beyond the natural beauty, I love the slice of local life it provides. You’ll see the local Koli fishing community bringing their boats in, which adds an authentic, rustic charm. I also find the area around the jetty fascinating, with the old Portuguese church and the visible naval base (INS Hamla) giving it a unique, historical flavor.
Marve also acts as a wonderful mini-adventure hub. The ferry service to Manori Island (famously known as Mini Goa) or Madh Island is a brilliant option for a quick, unplanned getaway. You can easily spend an hour relaxing here and then hop on a boat for a whole new experience.
Finally, you can't leave without indulging in the local treats. A small chaat stall offering spicy bhel puri or a perfectly roasted ear of corn makes the end of the evening perfect.
In my book, Marve Beach is a precious find. It’s a less commercialized, more tranquil space that provides a safe and picturesque backdrop for much-needed relaxation, making it my preferred coastal escape in the city. Just remember to visit on a weekday or early morning if you want the maximum peace, and leave the swimming to the fish—the strong currents here are no joke!

featured_reviews.review_text: This is the jetty to get a ferry to go for Padoda vipasna centre, essel world, water Kingdom and Gorai village. One can take a two wheeler in this ferry boat. This is a continuous up down ferry service for tourists and the villagers. Beautiful beach with a view suggested to go during a sunset and sunrise..
